notes: AP course names match the College Board's AP course list (apcentral.collegeboard.org/courses), checked 2026-10-25: all 40 AP courses (including exactly 8 world languages and the 2 AP Capstone courses), plus the 3 newer AP Career Kickstart courses (AP Business with Personal Finance, AP Cybersecurity, AP Networking), which are marked as newer because many schools don't offer them yet.

AP Physics 1 and 2 use the official names 'AP Physics 1: Algebra-Based' and 'AP Physics 2: Algebra-Based'. US History, US Government and the language courses also use official full names, with common short names (e.g. 'APUSH', 'AP Spanish') as search aliases.

Unsure: IB Environmental Systems and Societies was SL-only before the 2024 syllabus update, which added HL; both are listed. IB Latin is officially 'Classical Languages: Latin'. IB Theory of Knowledge has no SL/HL, so it uses the level 'IB'.

Regular/Honors/Dual Enrollment availability is set by each school; this catalog allows Honors for standard core courses and Dual Enrollment for upper-level core academic courses (where a local college class would normally replace the high school course).
Typical grades and prerequisites are common patterns, not rules — schools vary.
